questions: Did s-bend progress rise above 0.1675 at wheel_track 0.085 m, and did its max_error stay at or below 0.063 m?
Did steering_oscillation stay below 0.16 on the slalom and the s-bend? Slalom was 0.1574 and s-bend 0.1591 at 0.09 m. If either reached 0.16, what kp reduction do you recommend?
Did the oval hold progress near 0.17 and rms_error near 0.019?
Did any track complete? If not, which track ends off track first and at what progress?
Did line-loss events on the s-bend and slalom stay at one per run, or fall? Is the kp you used the same as iteration 9 (4.6)?
feedback_request.what_to_report: Per track (oval, s-bend, slalom): completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort, controller_errors. Also the kp that gave the best rms_error with this layout, and which sensors carry most signal when on the line.

intent: Continue the drivetrain test with a narrower wheel track of 0.085 m (from 0.09 m), holding the seven contiguous 16 mm sensors at x = ±0.048 m, y = 0.08 m, mass 0.8 kg, radius 0.03 m and body 0.12 × 0.16 m. Expected result: s-bend progress about 0.17 (above 0.1675), oval near 0.17 with line loss near 0.95, and slalom steering_oscillation between 0.155 and 0.165. If slalom or s-bend oscillation rises to 0.16 or above with line loss unchanged, the Integrator should reduce kp before any further geometry change, and the geometry fallback is wheel_track 0.09 m (the iteration 9 layout). If s-bend progress is flat at or below 0.1675, revert to 0.09 m and treat the drivetrain as exhausted at this sensing.
learning: Iteration 9 (wheel_track 0.09 m, kp 4.6) improved the s-bend from 0.1604 to 0.1675 and the oval from 0.167 to 0.174, with slalom oscillation 0.157 and s-bend oscillation 0.159, both just under 0.16. Slalom progress was flat at about 0.108. The drivetrain lever still gives small gains, but the oscillation margin is nearly used up. Forward lead (y = 0.08 m) and sensor pitch are exhausted as levers. Iteration 10 tests a midpoint step to 0.085 m, which keeps the oscillation risk down, and the next iteration will decide whether to keep it, revert, or stop changing geometry.
rationale: Iteration 9 (wheel_track 0.09 m, mass 0.8 kg, seven contiguous 16 mm sensors at x = ±0.048 m, y = 0.08 m) scored 61.75, up from 60.32 at 0.10 m. S-bend progress rose from 0.1604 to 0.1675 and the oval from 0.167 to 0.174. Slalom progress fell slightly, from 0.110 to 0.1075, and slalom steering_oscillation was 0.1574, just under the 0.16 trigger. S-bend oscillation was 0.159, also just under. Line loss stayed at one event per run on the s-bend and slalom and fell to 0.95 on the oval average, so sensing is not the limit. The drivetrain lever is still producing a small gain, but the oscillation margin is nearly gone. Lowering kp to 4.6 in that build held the effective turn gain roughly steady, so the oscillation near 0.157 reflects the same turn-rate level as iteration 8. The Integrator's rule applies: s-bend progress is above 0.1604 and slalom oscillation is below 0.16, so keep the layout and step the track narrower. I choose wheel_track 0.085 m, not the 0.08 m the Integrator named. Going from 0.09 to 0.08 m adds about 12 percent turn gain on top of unchanged kp, which would likely push slalom oscillation past 0.16 and waste the run. The midpoint keeps the test informative, with an expected s-bend progress of about 0.17 and slalom oscillation around 0.158 to 0.165. Sensing, forward offset, mass, body and radius stay as in iteration 9, so the result isolates the track width. The controller (kp) is left to the Integrator.
